questionText: The Board of Education of the Township of Boonton in the County of Morris, New Jersey (the “Board”) is authorized to (a) undertake various improvements, alterations, renovations, and upgrades at Rockaway Valley School, including but not limited to the construction of an addition and corridor expansion and renovations, reconfiguration and renovations of various existing classrooms, renovation and expansion of the science lab, renovations and ADA improvements to the art room and to the school nurse's facilities, upgrades and improvements to the HVAC system, replacement of the existing security system and fire alarm system, various electrical upgrades, replacement of windows in the Lower Gym, replacement of various portions of roofing, abatement of hazardous materials and related renovations, and lighting upgrades and new ceilings, including acquisition and installation of fixtures, furniture, equipment, and any site work; (b) appropriate $28,458,812 for such improvements; and (c) issue bonds in an amount not to exceed $28,458,812, and such bonds may only be utilized to fund the projects described in this Bond Proposal Question. The final eligible costs for the projects approved by the New Jersey Commissioner of Education are $21,185,538. The projects include $0 for school facility construction elements in addition to the facilities efficiency standards developed by the Commissioner of Education or not otherwise eligible for State support pursuant to N.J.S.A. 18A:7G-5(g). The State debt service aid percentage will equal 40% of the annual debt service due with respect to the final eligible costs of the projects. The Board of Education is authorized to transfer funds among the projects approved at this election. Do you approve this Bond Proposal Question?

questionText: Shall the Pequannock Township Council adopt an Ordinance revising the permitted uses of the Open Space, Recreation, Farmland and Historic Preservation Trust Fund, currently codified as Section 5-112 of the Pequannock Township Code, to allow the Open Space, Recreation, Farmland and Historic Preservation Trust Fund to broaden the purposes for which it may be used to include all purposes authorized by N.J.S.A. 40:12-15.7 specifically including the purpose of stewardship of permanently preserved land acquired for recreation and conservation purposes that are designed to restore or enhance its utilization for those purposes, and allow the use of previously collected funds for these purposes.
officialStatement: This proposal will give Pequannock Township greater flexibility in its use of the funds in its Open Space, Recreation, Farmland and Historic Preservation Trust Fund. A “Yes” vote will mean the voters want to maximize the purposes for which the fund can be used to include natural resource management, habitat restoration and wildlife stewardship as eligible activities on permanently preserved land acquired for recreation and conservation purposes in addition to other purposes within the limits allowed by state law. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST TO RAISE ADDITIONAL TAXES.

Shall the Pequannock Township Council adopt an Ordinance revising the permitted uses of the Open Space, Recreation, Farmland and Historic Preservation Trust Fund, currently codified as Section 5-112 of the Pequannock Township Code, to allow the Open Space, Recreation, Farmland and Historic Preservation Trust Fund to broaden the purposes for which it may be used to include all purposes authorized by N.J.S.A. 40:12-15.7 specifically including the purpose of stewardship of permanently preserved land acquired for recreation and conservation purposes that are designed to restore or enhance its utilization for those purposes, and allow the use of previously collected funds for these purposes.

This proposal will give Pequannock Township greater flexibility in its use of the funds in its Open Space, Recreation, Farmland and Historic Preservation Trust Fund. A “Yes” vote will mean the voters want to maximize the purposes for which the fund can be used to include natural resource management, habitat restoration and wildlife stewardship as eligible activities on permanently preserved land acquired for recreation and conservation purposes in addition to other purposes within the limits allowed by state law. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST TO RAISE ADDITIONAL TAXES.
